name: multicloud
description: Multicloud's customer-facing skills: point your own agent at your cluster and your cloud accounts, and keep the credentials on your machine.

metadata.description: Customer-facing skills for the Multicloud platform. Names reserved for the rest of the shelf are listed in README.md.

plugins.name: multicloud-advisor
plugins.description: Install the Multicloud Advisor into a Kubernetes cluster and connect to it over MCP, so your agent can price what you run today against every major cloud's spot and on-demand markets.

plugins.name: multicloud-connect-aws
plugins.description: Connect your AWS account to Multicloud: your agent runs mctl and OpenTofu/Terraform with your own AWS login, asks before it applies, and reports Ready or the missing permissions. It never sees your API key or the connect code.

plugins.name: multicloud-quota
plugins.description: Plan and request AWS quota increases for your Multicloud workloads: the agent asks what you want to run, reads limits, open requests and past denials, proposes an ordered list and files only what you approve.

plugins.name: multicloud-onboarding
plugins.description: Start with Multicloud from zero: your agent asks which door and which situation, runs the focused Multicloud skills in order, and keeps a resume ledger so the onboarding survives a quota wait of days.

plugins.name: multicloud-workstation
plugins.description: Prepare your computer for Multicloud: WSL2 on Windows, mctl, the AWS CLI, OpenTofu, kubectl and helm, the multicloud.io account and the mctl sign-in. You type every password yourself.

plugins.name: multicloud-aws-account-setup
plugins.description: Make a brand-new AWS account ready for Multicloud: root MFA, then IAM Identity Center single sign-on or an IAM user with a CLI key, and a working AWS CLI profile. The agent never sees a secret.

plugins.name: multicloud-extend
plugins.description: Give your own Kubernetes cluster cloud nodes or a cloud GPU with Multicloud Extend: cluster checks, pool, peering, connector install, and a first vLLM or burst workload, with the bundle read once and kept private.

plugins.name: multicloud-ci-pool
plugins.description: Run GitHub Actions jobs on machines in your own AWS account with a Multicloud CI pool: create the pool, connect GitHub, and run a first job with runs-on: multicloud.
